title: Pin the grade: mid-tone band, black point, ≤2% blown pixels
note: The default frame sits in a mid-tone band with almost nothing clipped to white; washed-out is measurable, not taste.
intent: "Washed-out / high-key / low-contrast" appeared in three separate judge notes and is measurable, not taste: the default frame’s mean luminance must sit in 0.32–0.45, no more than 2% of pixels may exceed 0.9 luma (the older 5% allowance is superseded), and the darkest 5% of pixels must fall below ~0.06 luma — a missing black point, not lamp intensity, is what reads as washed. Pin ACESFilmic tone mapping with toneMappingExposure ≈ 0.6–0.8 for reference-matched exteriors (≈ 0.35 with ambient ≤ 0.05 for BLAME!-style dark interiors) once at init, then touch only materials: darken the dominant large-area surface (water, sky, ground) to the reference mid-tone rather than re-tuning lights every iteration. A defect named twice must move a numeric parameter by ≥ 30%, not a nudge.

check.note: Default frame sits in the mid-tone band (mean luma 0.32-0.45) with at most 2% of pixels above 0.9 luma; washed-out / high-key is a measurable fail, not taste.

port: Call pinGrade() once from the mainOwner’s src/main.js at boot and never re-tune it in later iterations; when a verdict says washed or flat, change the base hex of the largest surface (water/sky/ground) by a visible margin and re-screenshot the same default camera. Log measureGrade() in state() so the numbers are in the evidence.

evidence.note: pin exposure/contrast once; no more than 5% of pixels above 0.9 luma (superseded by the 2% rule); fix the grade in one iteration, then only touch materials
scene mean luminance 0.32–0.45 and no more than 2% of pixels above 0.9 so washed-out is a measurable failure
black point: darkest 5% below ~0.06 luma; median luma 0.30–0.45; washed-out means the black point was never set
toneMappingExposure 0.6–0.8 for reference matches; ACES with exposure ≈0.35 and ambient ≤0.05 for dark interiors; change a named defect by ≥30%
contrast/grade gate: a washed-out build loses regardless of added geometry
